newsitem.title: UK: Spanish oranges flown to UK to avoid French strike.
newsitem.headline: Spanish oranges flown to UK to avoid French strike.

text.p: At least one British supermarket has chartered a Russian owned aeroplane in an effort to beat the French trucking strike and to replenish its shelves with Spanish fruit and vegetables.
Other supermarket chains are also chartering air space, some in the belly of passenger planes, to prevent the French trucker dispute leaving creating gaps in fresh fruit and vegetable shelves.

A large Russian made and owned Ilyushin Il-76 is due to land at Manston in Kent in south east England Wednesday afternoon with 40 tonnes of oranges from Valencia in Spain, a spokesman for AirRep UK Ltd who organised the airlift told Reuters.
On Tuesday, J. Sainbury Plc said it had chartered planes to bring fresh produce from Spain on Wednesday. A spokesman confirmed the flight to Manston was one of these.

Rival supermarket chain Tesco Plc on Wednesday said it was using Heathrow, Gatwick and Stansted to beat the truckers strike but declined to give details of flights. Two flights had come in on Tuesday and Tesco is expecting another one on Thursday, its spokesman said.

But supermarkets are having to compete in an already seasonally active air cargo market with major motor manufacturers facing serious assembly disruption as they try to bring together components made in different countries but normally trucked across Europe for assembly, airline and air cargo agents said.
AirRep are agents for Russian airline North East Cargo Airlines of Magadan, Russia who keep one Il-76 based at Manston. -- Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542 7706 Fax+44 171 542 5017
